text:
Ben Carter: Post-launch check-in thread for the benchmark report. Drop early metrics + what worked/didn’t + any surprises. Also need a decision on refresh cadence + what we want to change for the next iteration.

Tyler Benson: Pulling early numbers from GA + HubSpot + Amplitude. Snapshot as of this morning (last 36–40h):
- Landing page sessions: 38.4k (65% new)
- Report PDF downloads: 7.9k (20.6% LP->DL CVR)
- Redwood signups attributed (first-touch): 612
- “Book a consult” form submits: 84
- Demo/SE consult meetings scheduled (Salesforce): 41 (mix of inbound form + AE follow-ups)
- Top channels by sessions: organic 41%, paid search 19%, social 17%, partner referrals 9%, email 8%
- UTMs look clean except ~4% of social traffic missing utm_campaign (some employees sharing the raw URL)

Tyler Benson: Quality notes:
- Paid search CVR to download is lower (12%) but higher to consult (0.38%) vs organic (0.19%).
- EMEA traffic is over-indexing on FAQ + methodology appendix (avg time 2m+ higher). Probably good, but we should be ready for “data residency / region comparability” questions.

Camila Reyes: This is solid for day 2. :thumbsup: Any sign the “latency/$” headline is confusing people vs cost-only?

Soojin Lee: From social comments + a couple of inbound notes, the confusion is mostly: “is this $ per token?” and “why is lower latency per dollar better?” (lol). The explainer section is doing work but we can tighten the first 2 paragraphs + add a one-line definition near the hero chart.

Ethan Wallace: +1. Also a few readers interpreting it as a claim of absolute best across *all* workloads. The “what this does/doesn’t measure” callout is there, but people scroll past it.

Jordan Blake: From field: inbound quality is better than usual content launches. Most common first question on calls so far: “Can you map these numbers to *my* context (seq len + conc + region)?” Second: “Is this apples-to-apples w/ competitor X?”

Jordan Blake: The deck is landing well but AEs are asking for a simple qualification script:
- Region + data residency constraints
- Avg input/output tokens
- Concurrency/peak QPS
- Need for Dedicated/Private vs API
If we can put that in a 1-pager for SDRs, it’ll help.

Isabelle Laurent: Pipeline note: too early for hard influence numbers, but we already have 18 opps created with “Benchmark Report” campaign membership (HubSpot->SF sync). I’ll post a quick roll-up in #sales-ops later today.

Jasmine Liu: CS side: we had 9 existing customers ask “do these results reflect our dedicated cluster?” (they’re comparing their telemetry to the public table). We’re responding with: “public report is standardized harness; we can run a quick reproduction using your distributions.” But we should create a consistent macro + a short internal doc for CSMs.

Dev Patel: Support queue: 6 tickets tagged “benchmark” since launch. Two are basically “variance / confidence interval” questions.
- SUP-4921: prospect asking how many runs + rerun thresholds
- SUP-4938: customer sees region latency mismatch vs report; likely routing policy + time-of-day + their payload differences
We can handle, but would love one canonical “variance + why your numbers differ” paragraph we can paste.

Jonas Weber: Re: variance questions — we should publish a small addendum in the methodology appendix. Not raw runs, but:
- Number of repeats per model/region
- What we treat as acceptable run-to-run variance
- What gets rerun
Also we should explicitly call out: “these are steady-state windows under controlled load; your app may see different tail lat due to network + routing + prompt mix.”

Claire Dubois: +1. Also seeing people ask about caching/batching settings (“did you tune only for the benchmark?”). We did standardized configs, but we should add 3 bullets to make it explicit:
- warmup behavior
- prefix cache policy (on/off, size constraints)
- batching limits
We can keep it high-level without exposing anything sensitive.

Sana Farid: If we add anything about variance publicly, please avoid pseudo-precision. I’d recommend: “median with observed p95 range across repeats” (or a band) rather than claiming tight CIs unless we’re super confident in assumptions.

Elliot Price: Web note: we had a small hiccup yesterday w/ the download link caching (some users got a 404 for ~11 min). Fixed and purged CDN. INT-1192 is closed. If we do a v1.0.1 update to the PDF, we should version the file name + keep the existing URL stable.

Wei Chen: Docs/comments:
- The FAQ “Can I reproduce this?” section is getting traction.
- Biggest request: “give me the exact headers/region selection” (we have it but it’s a bit buried). I can move that snippet higher + add a short example request.

Renee Sullivan: Community angle: the “how to think about latency/$” framing is resonating w/ engineers, but the charts are intimidating for folks who just want a TL;DR. For the next iteration, can we add a “3 takeaways” card with plain language + link to the full tables?

Noura El-Khoury: Events/webinars: we can do a 30-min “office hours: interpreting the benchmark + reproducing on your workload” next week. That will soak up a bunch of questions and convert some of the high-intent folks.

Ben Carter: Great. On what *didn’t* work: besides the brief 404, anything?

Tyler Benson: Email nurture #2 (methodology deep dive) had lower CTR than expected (2.1% vs 3.4% target). Heatmap shows people bounced mid-email. Might be too dense / too many caveats upfront. Suggest we lead with a single figure + then “read methodology” for the folks who want it.

Soojin Lee: Agreed. Also, our LinkedIn post variants that used “cheaper” language got more engagement but worse downstream conversion (more comments, fewer clicks to download). The “production economics” + “predictable” language is converting better.

Jordan Blake: One more “didn’t”: a couple AEs paraphrased the headline too aggressively in outbound (“we’re #1”). We should re-send the do/don’t snippet + give them a safe one-liner.

Camila Reyes: Do it. Ben + Soojin, please send the reminder in #sales with the approved line + link to the enablement doc.

Ben Carter: Will do.

Camila Reyes: Refresh cadence decision: I don’t want us stuck in perpetual benchmarking, but we need enough frequency to stay credible. Proposal:
- Quarterly refresh of the public tables + PDF (aligned with major model/runtime changes)
- “Errata / minor copy updates” as needed (v1.0.1)
- Internal bench runs monthly for regression tracking (not public)
Thoughts?

Jonas Weber: Quarterly public refresh is reasonable. But we should also set a policy trigger: if we add a new region or materially change runtime defaults that affect latency/$, we should do an out-of-band refresh for the impacted subset.

Claire Dubois: +1. Also: for next iteration, I’d like to add one additional workload shape (long-context chat or tool/function calling). The current workload is representative, but people keep asking about longer outputs.

Sana Farid: If we expand workloads, we must keep comparability. Maybe we keep the current workload as the “baseline index” and add a second “long context” section explicitly not comparable to baseline.

Ethan Wallace: From narrative standpoint: baseline stays the hero. Add an appendix “additional workload: long context” with the same disclaimers.

Camila Reyes: Ok. Let’s lock:
1) Quarterly public refresh (target: early May for next full refresh)
2) Out-of-band subset refresh when we add a region / major runtime change / model lineup change
3) v1.0.1 addendum this week: variance language + caching/batching clarification + tighter latency/$ definition

Talia Benson: For process: I’ll schedule a 45-min retro next week (Marketing + Perf/Evals + Docs + Sales + Support). We’ll capture: what to keep, what to change, and owners for v1.0.1 + next run.

Dev Patel: +1 on v1.0.1. The support macro would benefit from a linkable “Why your numbers may differ” section.

Wei Chen: I can draft that section today and send to Jonas/Claire/Sana for review.

Ben Carter: Action items I’m capturing:
- Tyler: finalize early metrics snapshot + UTM cleanup note (employee sharing) + post in #marketing-ops
- Soojin/Ben: re-send approved claims one-liner + do/don’t to #sales
- Wei: draft “variance + why your numbers differ” + move region header example higher
- Jonas/Claire/Sana: review/approve variance wording for public doc
- Talia: schedule retro
- Noura: propose office hours agenda + date
Anything missing?

Jasmine Liu: Add CSM macro + internal doc. I can own that once Wei’s text is ready.

Elliot Price: When v1.0.1 is ready, please loop me in before publishing so we don’t break the stable URL again. We’ll do versioned PDF in storage + stable redirect.

Slackbot: Reminder set by Ben Carter to check early metrics again in 72 hours.

Tyler Benson: One last note: partner referral traffic (9%) is outperforming on consult conversion (0.62%). Might be worth nudging partners to send a second wave once we have v1.0.1.

Camila Reyes: Love it. Let’s keep momentum but stay disciplined on claims. The credibility is the product here.
